text:
Eden: hey everyone, first-week question. i'm on Ubuntu 22.04 (corporate laptop) and tried bootstrapping the dev env. installed asdf from git into ~/.asdf (per docs) and installed nodejs 18 + python 3.11, but `node -v` still prints the distro node (v12). asdf shims exist in ~/.asdf/shims. any quick fixes?
Carlos: welcome Eden! :wave: common issue is PATH ordering. what does `echo $PATH` show and do you start a login shell? asdf shims need to be before /usr/bin. also check you sourced asdf in the right shell init file.
Eden: PATH shows: /home/eden/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:... i have `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` in ~/.bashrc, but i ssh into the machine and start a non-login bash session via a warm script.
Carlos: try adding the source to ~/.profile or ~/.bash_profile so login shells pick it up. typical snippet we use in bash: 
```
# asdf
export ASDF_DIR="$HOME/.asdf"
[ -s "$ASDF_DIR/asdf.sh" ] && . "$ASDF_DIR/asdf.sh"
[ -s "$ASDF_DIR/completions/asdf.bash" ] && . "$ASDF_DIR/completions/asdf.bash"
```
Then open a fresh login shell or run `source ~/.profile` and `asdf reshim`. after that `which node` should point to ~/.asdf/shims/node.
Maggie: quick extra: if you also have Nix or direnv active they can mutate PATH unexpectedly. do you have a `/etc/profile.d/nix.sh` or a `.envrc` with `use nix`? that can put a different node earlier. run `type -a node` to see all candidates.
Eden: `type -a node` shows: node -> /usr/bin/node, /home/eden/.asdf/shims/node. so shim is after /usr/bin. i'm guessing some /etc/profile is exporting PATH later.
Carlos: yep. check /etc/environment and /etc/profile.d scripts. as a quick override you can export PATH in your ~/.profile so it comes earlier: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`. that forces shims first.
Maggie: also for python/venv in projects, prefer `python -m venv .venv` after `asdf install python 3.11.4` and `asdf local python 3.11.4` in the repo. for editor integration, if you use VSCode remote-ssh, make sure the remote server's shell init (often ~/.profile for remote sessions) loads asdf. opening VSCode from local GUI won't affect remote terminals.
Eden: thanks. another oddity: my dotfiles repo's `scripts/bootstrap` tries to create `~/.local/bin` and add a symlink `~/.local/bin/redwood` but fails with "Permission denied" even though the directory is owned by me. ls shows sticky bit on parent.
Maggie: sticky bit on /home/eden? run `ls -ld ~` and `lsattr -d ~/.local/bin`. sometimes company provisioning sets immutable attr. `sudo chattr -i ~/.local/bin` (if it was set) or contact infra if the home directory ACLs are managed. don't run the bootstrap with sudo.
Eden: noted. last question: quickstart mentions REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ENV in shellrc. don't want secrets in dotfiles. what's recommended?
Carlos: we recommend .env.local in the repo root (gitignored) plus a .env.example with placeholders. for per-shell secrets use direnv with .envrc that reads secrets from 1Password: e.g., `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(op item get "redwood/dev/api-key" --fields password)` if you have 1p CLI. direnv reduces the risk of committing secrets.
InfraBot: Hi Eden — internal git org invite and dotfiles access requested. Ticket INF-9021 opened to check corporate ACLs on home dir.
Eden: thanks all, i'll try exporting PATH in ~/.profile and check for nix/direnv conflicts. will ping if infra ticket reveals anything. cheers! :raised_hands:
